edges.judged_claim: In thermostat control systems, the Temperature Gap triggers heating. When the gap is positive (room too cold), the thermostat activates the furnace, causing an increase in Heating Rate. Larger gaps cause more aggressive heating, either through longer on-cycles (bang-bang control) or proportionally higher output (PID control). This is the core of negative feedback temperature regulation (ASHRAE 2017, Ch. 17).
